lotl.label: What's Going On With the Leafs
lotl.body: The Leafs' season has hit a hard patch, and Sunday's blanking made the warning impossible to ignore. Toronto fell 4-0 to New Jersey on Nov. 8, its third consecutive defeat after the 4-2 loss to Montreal, leaving the club 8-9, 10th in the Eastern Conference, with 18 points and nine games separating it from the top. The offense has gone quiet when it matters, while the blue line absorbed another blow: top prospect Ben Danford is week-to-week with a broken wrist, delaying a potential reinforcement just as the NHL roster needs one. At 0-4 against the Devils, there was no spark to hide behind and no late push to change the verdict. This is not panic territory, but it is no longer a harmless November wobble, either. Colorado arrives Tuesday at 7 p.m. ET on TSN, offering Toronto an immediate test of whether this slide is a slump - or the shape of the season.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Jays
lotl.body: Toronto's offseason has arrived with an uncomfortable truth: finishing 79-83 and second in the AL East was not enough, and the roster needs more than cosmetic repairs. Kazuma Okamoto's seventh-place Rookie of the Year finish, including one third-place vote and 17 points, offers a bright spot, but it also sharpens the question of how much help this lineup requires around him. The immediate pressure point is second base, where Ernie Clement's role may shift from regular to superutility player as Toronto searches for more offense. Then comes the grander swing: Tarik Skubal is expected to command the winter's biggest pitching market, and the Blue Jays are among the clubs linked to him, though the price could be ruinous. This is no time for half-measures. Watch the general manager meetings for Toronto's first serious move - an impact starter, a second baseman, or proof the club intends to stand pat.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Raptors
lotl.body: The Raptors' early-season promise is being tested by a roster held together with athletic tape. Monday's 118-102 loss to Memphis dropped Toronto to 5-5, fourth in the Atlantic Division, and extended its skid to one game - but the shorthanded club did not fold quietly. Ty Jerome's 27 points powered the Grizzlies, while Toronto played without Scottie Barnes, Immanuel Quickley, Collin Murray-Boyles and Kawhi Leonard, who missed his sixth straight game with left-knee swelling. Leonard's return to the bench offered a small sign of progress; his knee will be reevaluated in a week. That is not a timetable. It is a waiting room. The Raptors remain 3.5 games behind, and their margin for error is shrinking with every absent starter. Wednesday's 7 p.m. meeting with Boston will show whether Toronto can manufacture another fight - or merely survive until its stars return.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Commanders
lotl.body: The Commanders keep finding the same trapdoor: they battle hard, then falter when the game demands a clean finish. Sunday's 20-13 loss to the Rams dropped Washington to 2-5-1, left it third in the NFC East and extended the current skid to one game. The defense held its ground, but the offense was strangled by pressure - a sixth-round rookie was asked to block Myles Garrett, who returned to wreck the afternoon with three sacks. Jayden Daniels, working with a passing game thinned by injuries, could not summon a final answer. Treylon Burks missed the game with a foot injury, while cornerback Amik Robertson's ankle remains a Thursday question. There is no time for self-pity. Washington visits the Giants Thursday at 8:15 p.m. ET on Prime Video, with a chance to repair the damage from October's 27-27 tie and halt this season's slide.

article.title: Danford Injury Clouds Leafs Prospect Plans
paragraphs: The Leafs will face the Avalanche at 7:00 p.m. ET on TSN, with Blackwood projected to start for Colorado against Bobrovsky. Toronto enters at 8-9, while Rielly, Sissons and Roslovic are day-to-day with lower-body injuries. The organization also lost top prospect Ben Danford to a broken wrist; he is considered week-to-week.

The Jays are looking ahead after Kazuma Okamoto received Rookie of the Year votes, finishing with 17 points in the American League balloting. Toronto is also expected to be linked with Tarik Skubal this winter. The Raptors fell 118-102 to Memphis, despite Shead's 20 points and 11 assists and Poeltl's eight rebounds. They host Boston Wednesday at 7:00 p.m. ET.
The Commanders, 2-5-1 and third in the NFC East, visit the Giants Thursday at 8:15 p.m. ET on Prime Video. Toronto's next tip comes with Shead coming off a double-double.
